firstSourceAcceptance.status: Independently source-reviewed hypotheses; full current global consistency and host publication still required

sourceWitnesses.quote: 而幸根本之傾為趙倫之事

accepted.reason: The proposed merge is stronger than the Chinese. Chen Shu and Jinshu 127 share only the exemplum string 趙倫; Jinshu 127 does not write 司馬倫 in the cited unit, and Chen Shu does not identify 趙王 or 司馬. A merge may not rest on that string, Romanization, or the untrusted AD 301 rebel hints.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 賈謐乘惠皇之蒙昧，成此厲階，遂使悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷
尋先臣以剪除賈謐，封海陵公，事在淮南遇禍之前

accepted.reason: Each record writes the non-generic full personal name 賈謐. Jinshu 053 attests Jia Mi as the inner-palace favorite who slandered the crown prince; Jinshu 093 places the same 賈謐 on the stair of evil that destroyed Minhuai; Songshu 060 retrospectively names 賈謐 as the man cut down before the Huainan disaster. That is a full-name connection corroborated by the same Western Jin court catastrophe, not a title or Romanization merge.

possible-same-as understates an explicit alias. 053 states 南風，后名 of 賈后; 032 uses 南風 for the pepper-palace empress who destroys Jin. That is a source-attested name chain, not residual ambiguity. 032 does not itself write 賈南風.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草
或以潘岳《金穀詩序》方其文

accepted.reason: The four-way merge overreaches. 053 and 080 share attested 潘岳. Nanshi has only 安仁; Jinshu 117 has only 潘、陸. Those are not full personal-name connections, and Nanshi must not be described as writing 潘岳. Scope is reduced to the two 潘岳 records so the 117+songshu:073:p067 group is left intact.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 裴頠之於禮，任意而忽之

accepted.reason: All four write the non-generic full name 裴頠. Jinshu 053 shows him with Zhang Hua verifying the crown prince; Suishu quotes 《晉起居注》裴頠議 on temple ritual; Weishu 096 cites 裴頠 on the same ritual/mingtang problem; Weishu 091's 裴頠一室之議 is that ritual position reused in a later Bright Hall debate (邢臧 drafting it), i.e. retrospective mention of the same man. Romanizations are not the proof. weishu:091:p047 and weishu:096:p034 are already one canonical group and are not split.
Jinshu writes 衛瓘息庭 (surname 衛, given 庭). Jiu Tangshu writes 御史大夫韋挺 (surname 韋, given 挺). Different graphs in both surname and given name; English Wei Ting is not identity evidence.
Jinshu 衛瓘息庭 is not Xin Tangshu 攝刑部尚書韋挺. Different surnames 衛/韋 and given names 庭/挺; Romanized Wei Ting does not merge them.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯
以弟壺關侯武為淮陽王

accepted.reason: Jinshu names 洗馬劉務. Shiji names 子武為壺關侯, later 壺關侯武為淮陽王. 劉務 is not 武; English Liu Wu is a homonym only.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯

accepted.reason: Jinshu 劉務 is a Western Jin 洗馬. Shiji 淮陽王武 is a Han king named as the Young Emperor's brother. Different names 劉務 versus 武; this review does not adjudicate whether Shiji p070 and p139 are the same Han king.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣

accepted.reason: Jinshu 032 writes 衛瓘. Jinshu 101 quotes Confucius 微管仲, the Qi statesman 管仲. Different full names. The equivalent proposal against songshu:060:p117 (already in the 衛瓘 group) is the same name contrast and is not a background-only pair to reopen.

Jinshu 053's 武帝/武皇 is the Western Jin emperor who dotes on Minhuai (武帝愛之; 武皇鍾愛). Jiuwudaishi 067's 武皇 marries a clanswoman to 團 in a Five Dynasties biography. Shared temple/posthumous 武 is a reused title, not a personal-name connection.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 成都王穎之攻長沙王乂也
晉以宣王輔魏有功，立為高祖

accepted.reason: Jinshu 093 names 長沙王乂, the prince attacked by 成都王穎. Jiuwudaishi 142 names Jin's 宣王 established as 高祖 for meritorious aid to Wei—the already-merged Gaozu/Xuan King group, not 乂. Equivalent units that write 司馬懿 or 司馬宣王 still contrast with 乂; English Sima Yi is a homonym of 懿 versus 乂. The Gaozu group's other members are not pruned.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害

accepted.reason: Jinshu writes 臧, courtesy 敬文, second son of the crown prince, made 皇太孫, killed after 趙王倫篡位. Weishu writes 子藏，襲, then 齊受禪，例降—a later heir whose given name is 藏, not 臧. Different graphs, different fathers, different eras. English Sima Zang is not evidence.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 毛脩之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也

accepted.reason: Jinshu 臧字敬文 is the Western Jin imperial grandson 司馬臧. Songshu 毛脩之，字敬文 is a Xingyang man of a Mao lineage. Shared courtesy 敬文 without a full-name or alias chain is not a merge.
Jinshu 臧字敬文 is 司馬臧. Weishu 渾弟繪，字敬文 is Li Hui. Courtesy 敬文 alone does not identify them.

Supplied Chinese attests two different full personal names with no alias chain: 王戎 is appointed 太傅 among the crown prince’s 師傅 after 惠帝即位, while 鎮帥王熔 offers hostages in a Zhen-commandery campaign. Same Romanization and surname 王 do not identify them.

Chinese personal names differ (王戎 vs 王熔) with no attested identity link. 王戎 is a Western Jin 太傅; 鎮州王熔 is the Zhenzhou figure Li Cunxiao accuses of attaching to Bian. Homonymous English “Wang Rong” is not a merge.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 王鎔懼，以帛五十萬犒軍

accepted.reason: 王戎 and 王鎔 are distinct characters, not a supplied alias pair. 王戎 is named as 太傅 under 惠帝; 鎮州王鎔 campaigns against Xingzhou in the Jingfu narrative and later rewards Wuhuang’s army. No source chain equates them.
The Jinshu tutor 王戎 is not the 鎮州王鎔 to whom Wuhuang writes. Different given-name graphs 戎/鎔, different narrative settings, and no alias attestation.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 鎮州節度使王鎔來告難

accepted.reason: 王戎為太傅 is a different personal name from 鎮州節度使王鎔. The latter appears in a Bian/Baixiang war episode, not as an identity continuation of the Jinshu appointment. Keep-separate is required; this review does not merge or split other 王鎔 records.

The compared subject in Jiuwudaishi is 趙王镕, who appoints Li Lin and then 镕卒; that given-name graph 镕 is not 戎. 王戎 remains the Jinshu 太傅. No alias or same-person chain is supplied. The death notice concerns 镕, not the Jinshu man.
尚書令 is about to be granted to 趙州王镕 in a Liang Kaiping institutional note; that is not 王戎 the Jinshu 太傅. Names 戎 and 镕 differ, and no source equates them.
王戎 and 王融 share only surname 王 and English homophony. Nan Qishu names 中書郎王融 jesting with an envoy in the capital; Jinshu names 王戎 as 太傅. No alias is attested.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 遂攻鎮州，破臨城，王鎔來送款

accepted.reason: Xin Wudaishi 王鎔 comes to submit after the attack on 鎮州 and the fall of 臨城; Jinshu 王戎 is 太傅. Given names 戎 and 鎔 are different, with no identifying chain.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 本出中山相結，次子繼生洛州刺史暉

accepted.reason: Jinshu names 楊濟 as 太保 (and later 太子太傅楊濟). The Jiuwudaishi Yang genealogy cites 中山相結, i.e. a Zhongshan chancellor whose given name is 結, not 濟. English “Yang Ji” for both is Romanization only and is not an identity proof. No alias chain is supplied. This comparison is only 結 versus 濟; other Yang-genealogy descendants are not decided here.

held.reason: The supplied pair does not prove keep-separate. jinshu:032:s0301 深杜衛瓘之言 is the Jin statesman 衛瓘; nanqishu:016:s0025 晉惠帝初，衞瓘爲太保 uses the same personal name (衛/衞瓘) as Grand Guardian at the start of Emperor Hui's reign. That is a full-name plus office context match, so a split cannot be grounded in these units. nanqishu:016:p018 is already grouped with weishu:028:p004, whose Chinese is not in this packet; that member cannot be pruned, and a merge of the complete group cannot be checked without those units. Missing evidence: the weishu:028:p004 mention units (the proposal's AD 304–305 dating after 衛瓘's death is an untrusted hint until the Chinese is seen).

correction.before: Jia Nanfeng gave free rein to cunning and fanned disaster until it scraped the sky.
correction.after: South Wind gave free rein to cunning and fanned disaster until it scraped the sky.
correction.reason: The Chinese is only 南風肆狡，扇禍稽天。 The idiomatic English inserts the unattested compound Jia Nanfeng; 南風 is the name in the unit.

correction.before: But Xie Kangyue is unrestrained; his compositional form does not distinguish beginning from end. Pan Anren and Lu Shiheng are deeply worthy of reverence; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."
correction.after: But Kangyue is unrestrained; his compositional form does not distinguish beginning from end. Anren and Shiheng are deeply worthy of reverence; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."
correction.reason: The Chinese is 康樂, 安仁, 士衡, 顏延之. The literal English inserts surnames Xie, Pan, and Lu that are not in this unit.

correction.before: Lü Chao said, "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen Lin and Xu Gan of Wei, Pan Yue and Lu Ji of Jin."
correction.after: Lü Chao said, "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen and Xu of Wei, Pan and Lu of Jin."
correction.reason: The Chinese is 方敞魏之陳、徐，晉之潘、陸。 The idiomatic English supplies given names 潘岳 and 陸機 (and Chen Lin, Xu Gan) that this unit does not write.

correction.subject: jinshu:032:p179
correction.reason: Cited unit jinshu:032:s0303 writes only 南風, not 賈南風; certainty was marked explicit. The 南風 name is already claimed at jinshu:032:c0657.

correction.subject: jiuwudaishi:067:p117
correction.reason: The cited unit is 武皇愛之; the extraction stored an English personal name with null zh. The Chinese designation is 武皇.

correction.before: Again, Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Yang Clan Genealogy, saying: The Yang clan of Tang's Xingxing lineage descended from the house of the Duke of Yue, originally from Zhongshan Xiangjie; the second son Ji begot Hui, Prefect of Luozhou; Hui begot En, Administrator of Hejian; En begot Jun, the Respectful Duke of Yue, who moved out to dwell in Fengyi; down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
correction.after: Again, Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Yang Clan Genealogy, saying: The Yang clan of Tang's Xiuxing lineage descended from the house of the Duke of Yue, originally from Jie, Chancellor of Zhongshan; the second son Ji begot Hui, Prefect of Luozhou; Hui begot En, Administrator of Hejian; En begot Jun, the Respectful Duke of Yue, who moved out to dwell in Fengyi; down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
correction.reason: 中山相結 is office 中山相 plus given name 結, not a toponym “Zhongshan Xiangjie”. 修行 is Xiuxing, not Xingxing.

correction.before: Records of Travel and Official Service also gives the Yang Clan Genealogy: the Xingxing Yangs descended from the house of the Duke of Yue in Zhongshan; through Ji, Hui of Luozhou, En of Hejian, and Jun the Respectful Duke of Yue, who settled in Fengyi, down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
correction.after: Records of Travel and Official Service also gives the Yang Clan Genealogy: the Xiuxing Yangs of Tang descended from the house of the Duke of Yue, originally from Jie, Chancellor of Zhongshan; his second son Ji begot Hui, Prefect of Luozhou; Hui begot En, Administrator of Hejian; En begot Jun, the Respectful Duke of Yue, who settled in Fengyi, down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
correction.reason: The idiomatic line dropped 中山相結, fused 越公房 with Zhongshan, and used Xingxing for 修行. Restore chancellor Jie and the 次子繼生 sequence.

correction.subject: jiuwudaishi:128:p025
correction.reason: The unit names 結, whose English given-name rendering is Jie, not Ji (which collides with 濟/繼).

correction.subject: jiuwudaishi:108:p090
correction.reason: 镕卒 attests only that 镕 died. 復為王德明賓客 is Li Lin’s next post, not part of 王镕’s death.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 趙王镕辟為從事，镕卒，復為王德明賓客

notes: Jinshu 053 explicitly identifies 南風 as the empress's name (南風，后名) for 賈后, who persecutes the crown prince and is later 賈庶人. Jinshu 032, in the empresses-consorts chapter, names 南風 as the woman who first treads the pepper palace (初踐椒宮) and whose cruelty topples the state (南風熾虐，國喪身傾). That is the same rare personal name 南風 for the Western Jin empress, attested as an alias of 賈后 and corroborated by the same palace-destruction narrative, not a title-only or chronology-only link. The supplied 032 units never write 賈南風; the merge rests on 南風 plus empress context.

held.reason: Native validator rejects nickname-only shared alias on Jinshu032 side. Preserve independent source conclusion; do not downgrade to ambiguity or weaken gate. Correct actual name-kind claim with independent review before final publication.

notes: Only these two supplied records write the full personal name 潘岳: 黃門侍郎潘岳 drafting the forged prayer, and 潘岳《金穀詩序》 as a literary benchmark. nanshi:043:p016 writes 安仁, not 潘岳; jinshu:117:p239 writes only 晉之潘、陸. Courtesy-name-only or surname-plus-Lu literary pairing is not a merge, and the proposal's statement that Nanshi shares 潘岳 is false on the Chinese. jinshu:117:p239 stays with its already-merged companion songshu:073:p067; that group is not pruned and is not pulled into this merge.

whole67Renewal.reason: Removing the unsupported English-only local alias Sima Yi from jinshu:053:p006 does not change the title/name equation. Jinshu 001 identifies 宣皇帝諱懿，字仲達, then equates that subject with 宣王, 宣皇帝, and 高祖. Jinshu 053 still writes 太子似宣帝 of that ancestor; the Chinese 宣帝 is unchanged. The other 66 member signatures are stated unchanged. Entire 67-member membership is therefore still supported on the primary 懿–宣王–宣皇帝–高祖–宣帝 chain, without restoring the retired English local alias or altering dates.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 宣皇帝諱懿，字仲達，河內溫縣孝敬里人，姓司馬氏
武帝受禪，上尊號曰宣皇帝，陵曰高原，廟稱高祖
